change.author: Carina Wollendorfer

findings.title: Emails are sent using the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` decides, per attendee, between the new-guest email (`AttendeeScheduledEmail`) and the "guests added" email by `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (email-manager.ts:541). The handler filters the input down to `uniqueGuests` (line 74) and only those are inserted, but it passes the unfiltered `guests`. An address that was already an attendee and is re-submitted is in `guests`, so that existing attendee gets a fresh booking-confirmation email instead of the "guests added" notice. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

findings.title: Admin-or-owner check uses `&&`, so team admins are denied
findings.body: `isTeamAdmin` already matches role ADMIN or OWNER (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:270). `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` therefore reduces to owner only, and plain team admins fall through to the FORBIDDEN at line 55 unless they are also organizer or attendee. The variable name says "admin or owner". Use `isTeamAdmin` alone (or `||`). Also, when `eventType.teamId` is null this queries membership with teamId 0, which is a pointless DB round-trip; skip the check when there is no team.

findings.title: Server-side guest filtering is case-sensitive and does not de-duplicate the input
findings.body: The env blacklist is lowercased (line 71) but `guest` is compared as-is, so `Blocked@x.com` bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. The same case-sensitive comparison is used against existing attendees (line 76), so `A@x.com` is added beside an existing `a@x.com`. The uniqueness check exists only in the dialog's client-side zod refine (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26). The schema (addGuests.schema.ts:5) does not enforce it, so a direct tRPC call with duplicates inserts duplicate attendee rows. Lowercase the guests before filtering and de-dupe them (`new Set`) in the handler. Consider also a `.max()` on the array.

findings.title: Any attendee can add guests to any booking status, unlike the sibling editLocation
findings.body: `editLocation` goes through `bookingsProcedure` (util.ts:19-62), which limits access to the organizer or collective hosts. `addGuests` uses plain `authedProcedure` and also admits any attendee matched by `user.email` (line 52), with no limit on the number of guests. Each added address immediately receives a booking email with the event details. The handler also does not check booking status or time, so cancelled, rejected, pending or past bookings can be modified through a direct call, even though the UI hides the action in some of those states (BookingListItem.tsx:544-554). Please confirm attendee access is intended, and consider rejecting non-accepted or past bookings.

findings.title: `evt.team` is never set, so the team-member branch in sendAddGuestsEmails is dead
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends organizer emails to `calendarEvent.team?.members` (email-manager.ts:531), but the `CalendarEvent` built here has no `team`. For collective and round-robin bookings, the other hosts get no notification, and the code in the email manager never runs. Either populate `team` as the booking flow does, or drop the branch.

findings.title: Email failure is swallowed without logging the error; DB write precedes the calendar update
findings.body: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") }` drops `err`, so a failure cannot be diagnosed. Use the repo `logger`. Separately, guests are persisted (line 92) before `updateCalendarAttendees` (line 165). If that call throws, the client gets an error toast although the attendees were already saved, and no email goes out. The result of the calendar update is also ignored, so a failed calendar sync still reports "Guests added".

findings.title: Error toast fallback is unreachable and the message is not user-friendly
findings.body: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`` is always a non-empty string, so `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` never applies and the new `unable_to_add_guests` key is unused. For zod input errors `err.message` is a JSON blob, which would be shown verbatim after "BAD_REQUEST:". Show `t(err.message)` only for known handler codes and fall back to `unable_to_add_guests` otherwise.

findings.title: Schema rebuilt every render; invalid-state flag never cleared; closing via overlay/Esc doesn't reset
findings.body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is created inside the component on each render. Move it to module scope, or reuse the one in addGuests.schema.ts. `isInvalidEmail` is set at line 56 but only reset by Cancel. It stays visible after the user fixes the input or after a successful add. `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` closes the dialog on Esc or outside click without clearing `multiEmailValue` or `isInvalidEmail`, so stale input reappears when it is reopened. The duplicate check is also case-sensitive, so it disagrees with whatever the server does.

findings.title: Hardcoded English tooltip and dangling label association
findings.body: `content="Remove email"` is not passed through `t()`, unlike every other string in this component and the repo's i18n convention. Add a locale key. The `<label htmlFor="emails">` (line 21) refers to an id that no input has, so the label is not associated with any field. Pass an `id` to the first `EmailField`, or drop `htmlFor`.

findings.title: No tests for the new handler or the email manager function
findings.body: The PR adds a permission matrix (organizer, attendee, team admin/owner), filtering of blacklisted and duplicate guests, and a new email-selection branch, with no unit or e2e tests. Two of the defects above (the `&&` permission check and `guests` vs `uniqueGuests`) would be caught by a basic test of each.

contracts.action: Submit Add guests dialog -> trpc viewer.bookings.addGuests mutation
contracts.equivalent_path: editLocation mutation in BookingListItem via bookingsProcedure + editLocation.handler.ts
contracts.before_after: editLocation first runs bookingsProcedure, which restricts to organizer or collective host (util.ts:19-62), and updates the DB only after the calendar update succeeds (editLocation.handler.ts:107-126). addGuests uses authedProcedure with its own permission check, writes to the DB first (addGuests.handler.ts:92), then updates the calendar and sends emails.
contracts.visible_effect: Success toast, dialog closes, bookings list invalidated (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:36-41). The error toast is always prefixed with the code and the fallback message is unreachable.
contracts.failure_mode: If the calendar update throws after the DB write, the client sees an error but the guests are already saved. A failed email send is only console-logged; the user still sees success.

contracts.before_after: editLocation inspects the results and only writes and notifies when they are not all failures. addGuests ignores the return value. updateCalendarAttendees returns silently if there are no references, and updateAllCalendarEvents falls back to a DB credential lookup by reference.credentialId, so the acting user's credentials are not a blocker.
contracts.visible_effect: Calendar event gets the new attendees; failures are invisible to the user.
contracts.failure_mode: No-reference bookings and calendar errors are silent.

contracts.before_after: Selects the new-guest email by `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`. The handler passes unfiltered `guests`, not `uniqueGuests`, so already-present attendees can get a confirmation email.
contracts.visible_effect: New guests receive the AttendeeScheduledEmail; existing attendees receive AttendeeAddGuestsEmail; the organizer receives OrganizerAddGuestsEmail.
contracts.failure_mode: The team-member branch never runs because evt.team is unset; email errors are swallowed.

summary:
I found three wrong-today bugs in `addGuests.handler.ts` and several smaller issues. I only read the code and did not run anything.

**Fix:**
- **Wrong email list:** line 168 passes the raw `guests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of `uniqueGuests`. An address that is already an attendee gets the "scheduled" email again.
- **Admins locked out:** the permission check at line 48 combines `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner`. `isTeamAdmin` already includes owners, so only owners pass and plain team admins are refused.
- **Filtering gaps:** guest filtering is case-sensitive, so mixed-case addresses get past `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` (line 77). The server also doesn't de-duplicate the input, so a direct tRPC call can insert duplicate attendees.

**Consider:**
- **Auth and status:** `addGuests` is open to any attendee on a booking of any status, unlike `editLocation`.
- **Team hosts:** `evt.team` is never set, so the team-member branch in `sendAddGuestsEmails` never runs.
- **Error handling:** the email failure is swallowed without logging the error. The DB write happens before the calendar update.
- **Dialog:** the error-toast fallback in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43` is unreachable, and the dialog has stale-state problems.
- **`MultiEmail`:** it has a hardcoded English tooltip and a dangling label association.
- **Tests:** none were added.

I recorded three contract entries (the dialog mutation, the calendar update, the email send). All three are closed.
